Zuromin Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Żuromin, Poland

Demolished. Żuromin, dating to the late 13th century and granted Magdeburg rights in 1765, saw Jewish settlement begin in the early 19th century, initially under Kluczbork's synagogue supervision before independence in 1843; population reached 30.4% (415) by 1827, growing to 57% (1,959) by 1931. Germans burned the synagogue in September 1939 and deported residents to Nowy Dwór and Warsaw by November 8; some reached the Pomiechówek labor camp. Later concentration in Ciechanów District ghettos sent Żuromin's Jews mostly through Ciechanów and Mława to Treblinka and Auschwitz-Birkenau by November 1942. This cemetery, established in the first half of the 19th century (probably the 1840s) after independence from Kluczbork's cemetery, has documentation only from 1859 fencing records. Postwar abandonment lasted until 2009, when descendants and the Foundation for the Preservation of Jewish Heritage cleaned and fenced the site; a 2011 wall plaque names about 300 Jewish families who once lived in Żuromin.
